hints: Substitute point $A(1, 1)$ into the circle equation to get $a + b = 10$.
Substitute point $B(2, -6)$ into the circle equation to get $2a - 6b = -28$.
Solve the simultaneous equations to find $a$ and $b$.
Find the coordinates of the centre $\left(-\frac{a}{2}, -\frac{b}{2}\right)$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the coordinates of point $A(1, 1)$ into $x^2 + y^2 + ax + by - 12 = 0$:
$$1^2 + 1^2 + a(1) + b(1) - 12 = 0 \implies a + b = 10 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Substitute the coordinates of point $B(2, -6)$ into the circle equation:
$$2^2 + (-6)^2 + a(2) + b(-6) - 12 = 0 \implies 4 + 36 + 2a - 6b - 12 = 0$$
$$2a - 6b = -28 \implies a - 3b = -14 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1 to solve for $b$ and $a$:
$$(a + b) - (a - 3b) = 10 - (-14) \implies 4b = 24 \implies b = 6$$
$$a = 10 - 6 = 4$$

Find the centre of the circle using the standard formula for $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ where centre is $(-g, -f)$:
$$\text{Centre} = \left(-\frac{a}{2}, -\frac{b}{2}\right) = \left(-\frac{4}{2}, -\frac{6}{2}\right) = (-2, -3)$$

hints: Calculate the gradient of the radius $AC$ from the centre $C(-2, -3)$ to $A(1, 1)$.
Find the gradient of the tangent using the perpendicular relation $m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{m_{\text{radius}}}$.
Use the point-slope form with point $A(1, 1)$ and rearrange into $px + qy = k$ with integer coefficients.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gradient of the normal (radius $AC$) joining $C(-2, -3)$ and $A(1, 1)$:
$$m_{\text{radius}} = \frac{1 - (-3)}{1 - (-2)} = \frac{4}{3}$$

Use the perpendicular line property $m_1 m_2 = -1$ to find the gradient of the tangent line:
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{4/3} = -\frac{3}{4}$$

Write the equation of the tangent at $A(1, 1)$ using point-slope form:
$$y - 1 = -\frac{3}{4}(x - 1)$$

Multiply across by $4$ and rearrange into the required integer form $px + qy = k$:
$$4(y - 1) = -3(x - 1) \implies 4y - 4 = -3x + 3$$
$$3x + 4y = 7$$
